---
title: "Part 4 · The DPprior principle"
---

State a design-conditional target, calibrate Gamma(a, b) to it, diagnose the implied
weights, and decide whether a Dual-Anchor refinement is needed. Start with
[the workflow](workflow.qmd) (C-13), which walks the six steps with the paper's J = 50 example,
or with [the worked example](worked-example-j50.qmd) (C-15), which shows the three priors on
one strip.

## 1 State the target

| Page | Catalog | What it shows |
|---|---|---|
| [From what you expect to a prior](elicitation.qmd) | C-05 | An interval, a confidence level or a CV becomes (mu_K, sigma^2), then Gamma(a, b) and a dominance check; STAR triggers at .510 |
| [Where a Gamma prior exists](feasibility.qmd) | C-06 | The (mu_K, sigma^2) plane: below the profile bound (4.52 at mu_K = 6.5, J = 100) no Gamma prior, above (mu_K − 1)(J − mu_K) no count; drag a target |

## 2 Calibrate with TSMM

| Page | Catalog | What it shows |
|---|---|---|
| [Calibrate a count target](calibrator.qmd) | C-02 | Live TSMM: a target (mu_K, sigma^2) at J gives Gamma(a, b) in milliseconds, or the reason it cannot |
| [Stage 1, then Stage 2](stage1-stage2.qmd) | C-07 | The J = 50 example: A1 start (2.667, 2.608), five Newton steps to (1.4082, 1.0770) over the contours of the moment error, R and browser |
| [TSMM checked against R](tsmm-parity.qmd) | C-01 | Ten calibration targets solved in R and in the browser; the infeasible one refused by both |
| [Why the exact computation is cheap](why-fast.qmd) | C-10, C-12, C-11 | K_J is a sum of Bernoulli draws (the convolution equals the Stirling pmf), the Gamma mixture is a finite sum, and a TSMM solve takes milliseconds |
